decisions.why: Carried forward; text unchanged. FR-001 asks the same reading of the two nested files for the checks that work there.

decisions.summary: A moved rule is written once, short, in the contract's own voice, in the section that already covers its subject or under a House rules heading.
decisions.why: Carried forward; text unchanged. FR-001 asks for the contract's own voice and no longer than the check needs.

decisions.why: Carried forward; text unchanged. FR-003's setting, method and rule.

decisions.summary: Root CLAUDE.md's review-subagents bullet gains a sentence; docs/efficiency-tooling.md's feature-255 row gains the outcome; review-ledger untouched.
decisions.why: Carried forward; text unchanged. FR-006 names those documents and no other.

decisions.summary: Amendment 1 edits two guard files - .claude/skills/diagram/tests/test_agent_models.py (the field's test, P6) and the skill Makefile (make scatter-bases, P8) - each with GUARD_EDIT_OK and a reason, where the first landing edited none.
decisions.why: FR-007 asks for the requirement in test_agent_models.py by name ('which already derives its roster from .claude/agents/') and FR-009 asks for a make target wrapping the scatter parse; the Makefile and that test are guard files, so guard-file-hooks.sh requires the escape. Nothing is being excepted: the escape is the repository's own route for an edit the spec demands, and the line records which two files and why.

decisions.summary: The Route line is left at DIRECT although Amendment 1's delta now reaches the skill Makefile, tests/test_agent_models.py and scripts/.
decisions.why: The route is chosen from the delta by the repository's rule - engine code is l7r/**/*.py and pool/*.gen.py|*.json - and none of the amendment's paths are engine code, so DIRECT still holds. The enumeration in the Route line is now incomplete as prose (it lists .claude/agents/, root CLAUDE.md, docs/, specs/), but the decision it records is unchanged and correct.

decisions.summary: One test in test_agent_models.py, test_every_agent_launches_without_the_claude_md_files, requiring the field of every file in the already-derived roster, with a message naming the field, the GM's ruling and the feature; the module docstring gains the ruling; the tier table is untouched.
decisions.why: FR-007 word for word: the module that already derives the roster 'also requires omitClaudeMd: true of every agent file, so an agent added later launches without the three files or the gate fails'. Deriving from the roster rather than a hand list is what makes a LATER agent file fail, which is the clause's own purpose. Leaving the tier table alone keeps the amendment to what was asked.

decisions.summary: The guard is proven by removing the field from one file and watching the test go red, and root CLAUDE.md's gate row for test_agent_models.py gains a clause naming what it now enforces.
decisions.why: The red proof is FR-007's second sentence verbatim. The CLAUDE.md row is a one-clause documentation edit to a row that already exists for this very file, recording an enforcement the GM asked for; it adds no behavior and no scope, and the repository's own rule is that every guard appears in that table.

decisions.summary: spec-fidelity.md question 4's 'extra verification the GM did not request' becomes 'verification of something the GM did not ask for', with a paragraph after question 5 stating the distinction on this feature's round 1 as the worked example; spec-fidelity-verify.md gains the same paragraph.
decisions.why: FR-008 asks that BOTH fidelity contracts carry the GM's distinction and identifies question 4's phrase as the sentence that caused the cut. The rewording is the minimum edit that removes the trap, and the paragraph carries both halves FR-008 names (what serves the request, and what stays out of scope - unrequested verification, and new behavior riding in under the name of a check).

decisions.summary: The fidelity-contract change is proven by ONE seeded run: dispatch_seeded.sh on round 1's own recorded prompt, the tree at the spec's first commit, the amended contract copied in, scored on four items - old FR-003 must not be cut, and the failure branch, the memory-index sentence and SC-004 must still be raised. No control leg and no second case.
decisions.why: This is FR-008's own sentence ('the amended contract is run on round 1's own recorded prompt, and it must no longer cut old FR-003 while still raising that round's other three items') and the repository's stated method for improving a review agent ('add the general rule, prove it fires on the unfixed artifact, then fix the artifact') - one run on the unfixed artifact is that method, not a reduction of it. A control leg is FR-003's rule for the FIELD proof, where the question is whether removing three files costs a finding; here the control already exists in the record - round 1's verdict is what the UNAMENDED contract returned on this same prompt, and it is the thing the run must differ from on exactly one item and match on three. The four scored items are round 1's four items exactly, as the spec's Review history records them, so nothing of that round is dropped.

decisions.summary: make scatter-bases MAP=<pool map> is added to the skill Makefile (GUARD_EDIT_OK, a new read-only diagnostic) running l7r.diagram.tools.scatter_audit on the map's SVG, and settlement-review's paragraph names the target; the three (Tools: ...) description tails are cut; the seven contracts citing tests/test_agent_models.py cite .claude/skills/diagram/tests/test_agent_models.py.
decisions.why: FR-009 asks precisely for 'a make target wraps it and the contract names the target', plus the two cosmetic fixes the GM listed. The GM's words are 'fix anything left unfixed, including the settlement-review issue ... and the two cosmetic path and description duplications'; a make target is the repository's only sanctioned route to an engine entry point, so wrapping rather than giving the module a new CLI is the literal fix and adds no behavior beyond a read-only diagnostic. HOW the recipe reaches parse_bases (inline, or through a helper script under scripts/) is drafting the plan does not decide; the working tree currently adds scripts/_scatter_bases.py with its own test, which is still within FR-009 but is not recorded in this plan text - if the plan is amended to say so, the digest moves and a fresh verdict is owed.

decisions.summary: The six agents with recorded runs are paired on named recorded cases: entry-drift farmhouse (251 R5), escalation-check 242 (251 R5), quote-check capitals fn-235..240 with its make quote-verbatim report (255 R2), source-applicability Shanghai (255 R1), source-reader 09-12 with its saved pages (255 R4), spec-fidelity feature 251's MODE 2 round 1.
decisions.why: FR-010 asks for exactly these six agents 'each on one recorded case with known findings'. Each case named is a row of the cited record with its own findings - checked: 251 R5 carries 'entry-drift farmhouse ... DRIFTED' and 'escalation-check 242 ... 3 KEEP, 1 REWRITE, 2 CUT'; 255 R2 carries 'quote-check, capitals fn-235..240 (6 notes) | fn-237 NOT-ON-PAGE at its link, and "23" in no quote'. The phrase 'cut to a slice where the recorded run was large' describes cases the RECORD already scored as slices (255 R2 scored the capitals slice on its own findings), which keeps FR-003's 'recorded prompt, verbatim' intact; a slice the record does not carry would not, and the plan does not propose one.

decisions.summary: building-review is paired on tests/fixtures/ochiba-no-scale-red.svg (scale bar removed) and size-audit on tests/fixtures/ochiba-big-bath-red.svg (an oversized bath), each staged in a HEAD worktree as a pool subject pool/magistracies/ochiba-red/ beside a copy of the Ochiba magistracy's notes and rendered to PNG.
decisions.why: FR-010 asks for exactly this: 'each on a frozen defective sheet under tests/fixtures/ whose defect is known by construction', scored against the CONTROL first by FR-003's rule. Both sheets are known by construction and are the defect each agent's own contract names ('Scale bar -> REQUIRED ... If ABSENT -> ERROR'; an oversized fixture rect of 90x90 px against the sheet's 40x33). The borrowed notes do not contaminate the pair: the two fixtures ARE the Ochiba magistracy sheet with one line changed (diff against pool/magistracies/ochiba-magistracy/ochiba-magistracy.svg is a single rect in one and the scale-bar text in the other), so the copied notes are that sheet's OWN notes rather than a stranger's; the notes' Review log settles the divider gate, the pond and the cell size and nothing touching the scale bar or the bath - it records the bath at 13x11 ft, which makes the injected defect easier to see, not laundered; and both legs of each pair carry identical staging, so anything the notes add appears in the control too and FR-003's control-first rule absorbs it. Staging in a scratch worktree leaves the clone's pool/ untouched, as SC-005 requires.

decisions.summary: All eight pairs run by FR-003's harness and rule with FR-004 governing a miss; sixteen runs, the batch's size stated before launch; settlement-review and perf-audit are priced in research.md with their reasons.
decisions.why: FR-010 says every pair is run by FR-003's method and scored by FR-003's rule, and that the two left out are put to the GM with their particular reasons and prices, not decided by the session; T10 carries 'priced for the GM'. Two restatement gaps to honor from the spec rather than the plan, neither a decision to do otherwise: FR-003 asks that the batch's size AND its rough weight be stated before launch, where P9 says size only; and FR-010's 'put to the GM ... the eight results in hand' means the question reaches the GM, not only research.md.
It follows FR-007 to FR-011 in order and puts the guard and the contract change before the sixteen runs and the landing gate; tasks.md T07-T11 name the same work with the same requirement ids.
